Ezk.16.structure: Found in blood, adorned, given cities, then trusting her beauty and paying lovers, ending in restoration.
Ezk.16.world_behind: Brides were washed, anointed and given jewellery; harlotry here means political alliances sealed with tribute.

deep_background.note: Newborn exposure was common in the ancient world, which makes the rescue image sharper.

Ezk.17.occasion: Two eagles and a vine explain the Babylonian treaty.
Ezk.17.structure: The first eagle plants the vine, the vine reaches for a second, the oath is broken, God replants it himself.
Ezk.17.world_behind: Zedekiah swore loyalty to Babylon in the LORD's name, so revolt was covenant-breaking, not only politics.

deep_background.note: An oath taken before the deity bound the whole nation, which is why the prophet condemns it.

Ezk.18.occasion: The proverb about sour grapes is answered.
Ezk.18.structure: The soul that sins dies, three case studies of the righteous and wicked, then a call to repent.
Ezk.18.world_behind: Exiles blamed their parents' generation, so the prophet answers the complaint of inherited guilt.

deep_background.note: Repentance is described as a change of conduct, not merely regret, matching the covenant lawsuit form.

Ezk.19.occasion: A lament for the last kings of Judah.
Ezk.19.structure: Lioness and cubs, then a vine burned in the wilderness, sung as a dirge.
Ezk.19.world_behind: Josiah's sons were taken to Egypt and Babylon, which the two halves of the lament recount.

deep_background.note: Royal lion imagery comes from Genesis 49 and was stamped on Judah's own weights and seals.

Ezk.20.occasion: Israel's history is retold as a record of rebellion.
Ezk.20.structure: The elders are refused, then four cycles from Egypt to the wilderness to Canaan, ending in mercy.
Ezk.20.world_behind: Sabbath observance is treated as the covenant sign that Israel repeatedly defiled.

deep_background.note: God spares Israel for the reputation of his own name among the watching nations.

Ezk.21.occasion: The sword of the LORD is drawn against Jerusalem and Ammon.
Ezk.21.structure: Sword song, the king of Babylon casting lots at the fork, then Ammon's own judgment.
Ezk.21.world_behind: Divination by arrows, teraphim and liver inspection was standard before a campaign, shown here under God's control.

deep_background.note: The omen fell for Jerusalem, meaning the siege was decided before a single engine rolled.

Ezk.22.occasion: Jerusalem is indicted as a bloody city.
Ezk.22.structure: A catalogue of sins, then dross in the furnace, then the search for one who would stand in the gap.
Ezk.22.world_behind: Bloodshed, usury and oppression of the resident alien were covenant crimes with named penalties.

deep_background.note: Intercession is pictured as a man standing in a breached wall, the same image used of Moses.

Ezk.23.occasion: Two sisters, Samaria and Jerusalem, are tried as unfaithful wives.
Ezk.23.structure: Oholah and Oholibah, their alliances with Assyria and Babylon, then the cup of judgment.
Ezk.23.world_behind: Treaties were sealed with tribute and sometimes with the exchange of sacred objects, read here as adultery.

deep_background.note: Drinking a cup of judgment is a fixed prophetic image for receiving the full penalty.

Ezk.24.occasion: The siege begins and Ezekiel loses his wife as a sign.
Ezk.24.structure: The boiling pot parable, then the death of the prophet's wife and the command not to mourn.
Ezk.24.world_behind: Mourning rites were public and loud; refusing them made the prophet himself a visible sign.

deep_background.note: The temple and the wife are both called the delight of the eyes, linking personal grief to national loss.

Ezk.25.occasion: Oracles against Ammon, Moab, Edom and Philistia.
Ezk.25.structure: Four short verdicts, each for gloating over Jerusalem's fall.
Ezk.25.world_behind: Neighbouring states profited from Judah's collapse by taking land and trade routes.

deep_background.note: Clapping and stamping over a rival's ruin was a formal gesture of contempt, not private spite.

Ezk.26.occasion: Tyre is sentenced for rejoicing at Jerusalem's ruin.
Ezk.26.structure: The city becomes a bare rock, its stones thrown in the water, its princes in mourning.
Ezk.26.world_behind: Tyre was an island fortress and the Mediterranean's great trading port, thought impregnable.

deep_background.note: Alexander later scraped the mainland city into the sea to build a causeway, matching the image.

Ezk.27.occasion: A lament over Tyre as a magnificent ship.
Ezk.27.structure: Ship's timbers and crew catalogued, cargo list of nations, then the shipwreck.
Ezk.27.world_behind: Tyre's wealth came from cedar from Lebanon, linen from Egypt and metals from Spain.

deep_background.note: The list doubles as a trade map of the ancient Mediterranean world in the sixth century.

Ezk.28.occasion: The king of Tyre is judged for claiming divinity.
Ezk.28.structure: The prince's pride, the guardian cherub's fall, then Sidon's judgment and Israel's restoration.
Ezk.28.world_behind: Tyre's king was honoured as divine in local cult, and the city's wealth backed the claim.

deep_background.note: The cherub imagery behind the fall of a proud ruler shaped later teaching on pride and fall.

Lam.1.occasion: Jerusalem sits widowed and desolate after the fall.
Lam.1.structure: Acrostic grief: the city personified, her allies gone, her children taken.
Lam.1.world_behind: A besieged capital lost its trade, its temple and its population in one generation.

deep_background.note: A city stripped of defenders was described as a widow, left without protection.

Ezk.29.occasion: Egypt is judged as a river monster that failed its ally.
Ezk.29.structure: Pharaoh the dragon of the Nile, forty years of scattering, then Egypt restored but diminished.
Ezk.29.world_behind: Egypt was the great power Judah kept trusting instead of Babylon, and it never delivered.

deep_background.note: Egyptian art pictured the Nile as a serpent to be speared, imagery the prophet turns against Pharaoh.

Ezk.30.occasion: The day of the LORD against Egypt and its allies.
Ezk.30.structure: Wailing for the day, the sword at Egypt's borders, the arm of Pharaoh broken.
Ezk.30.world_behind: Nebuchadnezzar's 568 BC campaign reached Egypt, matching the prophecy's horizon.

deep_background.note: Breaking the arm meant destroying military strength, a common treaty-curse image.

Ezk.31.occasion: Egypt is compared to Assyria as a cedar felled for pride.
Ezk.31.structure: The cedar's height and waters, its fall to the nations, then descent to the pit.
Ezk.31.world_behind: Cedars of Lebanon stood as the ancient world's image of unmatched height and glory.

deep_background.note: Comparing a king to Eden's trees links political pride to the oldest story of grasping for height.

Ezk.32.occasion: A lament over Pharaoh as a lion and a sea monster.
Ezk.32.structure: Two laments, a month apart, ending with Egypt among the uncircumcised in the pit.
Ezk.32.world_behind: The pit and Sheol were imagined as the place of the dead, entered by all nations alike.

deep_background.note: The roll call of fallen nations makes the point that no empire escapes the same end.

Ezk.33.occasion: The watchman charge is restated and the city's fall is reported.
Ezk.33.structure: Watchman duty, the fairness of God's dealings, the fugitive's news, then the people's empty listening.
Ezk.33.world_behind: The messenger who escaped Jerusalem arrived months later, anchoring the vision to a date.

deep_background.note: The people enjoyed the prophet's voice without obeying him, a warning about listening without doing.

Ezk.34.occasion: Shepherds are condemned and the one Shepherd promised.
Ezk.34.structure: False shepherds judged for feeding themselves, then God shepherding, then the prince among them.
Ezk.34.world_behind: Kings were routinely called shepherds across the ancient Near East, from Hammurabi to Assyria.

deep_background.note: Even the flock is judged for trampling the pasture, so privilege carries its own indictment.

Ezk.35.occasion: Mount Seir, Edom, is judged for profiting from Judah's ruin.
Ezk.35.structure: Edom's hatred and claim on the land, then its desolation.
Ezk.35.world_behind: Edom occupied the Negev and the Judean south after 586 BC, taking land while the exiles were gone.

deep_background.note: Edom's rivalry began with Jacob and Esau, and the prophets treat it as a family betrayal.

Ezk.36.occasion: The mountains of Israel are restored and the new heart promised.
Ezk.36.structure: The land's restoration, then the gathering, the cleansing water and the heart of flesh.
Ezk.36.world_behind: The land had lain empty for decades, reclaimed by neighbours, so restoration was a property claim too.

deep_background.note: Cleansing with water then a new spirit follows the pattern of covenant renewal and later baptismal imagery.

Ezk.37.occasion: The valley of dry bones and the two sticks.
Ezk.37.structure: Bones raised by the word and the breath, then Judah and Ephraim joined into one stick under one king.
Ezk.37.world_behind: Bones left unburied were the ultimate curse, so a valley of them meant total national death.

deep_background.note: The same Hebrew word means breath, wind and Spirit, so resurrection and renewal are one act here.

Ezk.38.occasion: Gog of Magog invades the restored land in the latter days.
Ezk.38.structure: The coalition gathered, God's hook in Gog's jaw, the earthquake and the rout.
Ezk.38.world_behind: Magog appears in Assyrian records as a distant northern people, so the name means the far threat.

deep_background.note: The image says the invader is dragged to the field by God rather than choosing the timing.

Ezk.39.occasion: Gog's defeat and the great feast for the birds.
Ezk.39.structure: Weapons burned seven years, bodies buried at Hamon-gog, the feast, then Israel regathered.
Ezk.39.world_behind: After battle, unburied dead defiled the land, so a named burial site was a cleansing requirement.

deep_background.note: Burning the enemy's weapons instead of wood shows the scale of the arsenal left behind.

Ezk.40.occasion: A vision of the restored temple begins with measurements.
Ezk.40.structure: The prophet set on a high mountain, a man with a measuring reed, the gate, the outer court, the inner court.
Ezk.40.world_behind: Temple plans were given in writing and measured by reed, as Babylonian building records also show.

deep_background.note: Measurement means the plan is fixed and certain, the same device used in Revelation 11.

Ezk.41.occasion: The nave, side chambers and altar are measured.
Ezk.41.structure: Inner house dimensions, the carved cherubim and palms, the wooden altar.
Ezk.41.world_behind: Palm and cherub carvings echo Solomon's temple, tying the vision to the earlier sanctuary.

deep_background.note: Cherubim guarded the way to God, so carving them on the walls repeats the boundary idea.

Ezk.42.occasion: Priestly chambers and the outer wall are measured.
Ezk.42.structure: Chambers for changing and eating, the separating wall, the total square.
Ezk.42.world_behind: Priests changed garments between holy and common space, a practical as well as symbolic boundary.

deep_background.note: The wall's function is separation of realms, the organising idea of the whole vision.

Ezk.43.occasion: The glory of the LORD returns to the temple.
Ezk.43.structure: Glory enters by the east gate, the throne described, the altar consecrated with offerings.
Ezk.43.world_behind: The east gate faced the sunrise and the exile road, so the glory came back the way it left.

deep_background.note: The earlier departure in chapter 10 is answered here, closing the book's central loss.

Ezk.44.occasion: The east gate is shut and priestly duties are ordered.
Ezk.44.structure: The closed gate, the prince's standing place, Levites demoted, Zadokite priests honoured.
Ezk.44.world_behind: Gate privileges marked rank in ancient cities, so a permanently shut gate was a statement about holiness.

deep_background.note: Zadok stayed faithful when others fell, which explains why his house keeps the altar.

Ezk.45.occasion: The holy district and the prince's portion are assigned.
Ezk.45.structure: The sacred allotment, the city's land, the prince's inheritance, then just weights and offerings.
Ezk.45.world_behind: Land allotments were the basis of wealth and identity, so the district defines the new order.

deep_background.note: Honest ephah and bath are required alongside worship, joining commerce to holiness.

Ezk.46.occasion: The prince's worship and the temple kitchens.
Ezk.46.structure: East gate on sabbaths, the prince's offerings, the people's movement through the courts, the boiling places.
Ezk.46.world_behind: Crowds entered and left by separate gates to keep order during festivals.

deep_background.note: Sacrifices were cooked inside the complex so the holy meat never left the sacred area.

Ezk.47.occasion: A river flows from the temple and the land's borders are drawn.
Ezk.47.structure: Water deepening from ankles to a river, trees on both banks, then the boundary lines.
Ezk.47.world_behind: Jerusalem has no river, so the vision is a deliberate reversal of geography and of Eden's river.

deep_background.note: The river sweetens the Dead Sea, which is the strongest possible image of life from death.

Ezk.48.occasion: The tribal portions are assigned and the city gets its name.
Ezk.48.structure: Twelve strips of land, the city's square, the gates named for tribes, then the closing name.
Ezk.48.world_behind: Each tribe receiving a strip from north to south mirrors the ideal allotment under Joshua.

deep_background.note: The book ends with the city named 'The LORD is there', answering the loss of the glory at the start.

Dan.1.occasion: Four Judean youths are taken into Babylon's service.
Dan.1.structure: Deportation, renamed, the food test, then wisdom granted beyond the court's experts.
Dan.1.world_behind: Court training involved language, literature and a new name, absorbing the exile into the empire.

deep_background.note: The request avoided meat offered to idols and wine, a stand taken at personal cost.

Dan.2.occasion: Nebuchadnezzar's dream of the statue is interpreted.
Dan.2.structure: The dream demanded, prayer answered, the image of four metals, the stone that fills the earth.
Dan.2.world_behind: Babylonian diviners read dreams from omen texts but could not supply a forgotten dream.

deep_background.note: The kingdom that replaces the empires is described as unbuilt by human means.

Dan.3.occasion: Three youths refuse the golden image.
Dan.3.structure: The image erected, the refusal, the furnace heated sevenfold, the fourth figure, the decree.
Dan.3.world_behind: Imperial images were loyalty tests; refusing to bow read as political rebellion, not private belief.

deep_background.note: The extra figure is described as a son of the gods, the first hint of divine presence in the book.

Dan.4.structure: The tree vision, its interpretation, twelve months of pride, the humbling, then restoration and praise.
Dan.4.world_behind: Babylonian texts describe a king's withdrawal and recovery, though not this confession.

deep_background.note: The decree is issued by watchers, the book's term for angelic mediators of judgment.

Dan.5.occasion: Belshazzar's feast and the writing on the wall.
Dan.5.structure: Sacred vessels used in a drunken feast, the writing, Daniel's reading, the fall that night.
Dan.5.world_behind: Belshazzar was a co-regent while Nabonidus campaigned abroad, which fits his offer of third place.

deep_background.note: The three words are weights and divisions, so the sentence is delivered in commercial units.

Dan.6.occasion: Daniel in the lions' den under Darius.
Dan.6.structure: Envy, the decree trapping the king, the night in the den, deliverance, the accusers' fate.
Dan.6.world_behind: Persian law was held irrevocable, which is why the king could not cancel his own decree.

deep_background.note: Prayer facing Jerusalem three times daily follows the pattern later codified in Jewish practice.

Dan.7.occasion: Four beasts rise and the Ancient of Days takes the throne.
Dan.7.structure: Sea beasts, the little horn and the saints, the judgment scene, the son of man given dominion.
Dan.7.world_behind: The sea in ancient myth is chaos, so beasts from the sea are empires born from disorder.

deep_background.note: The figure given eternal dominion is the source of the title Jesus used for himself.

Dan.8.occasion: The ram and the goat vision at Susa.
Dan.8.structure: Medo-Persia as a ram, Greece as a goat, the four horns, the little horn exalting itself.
Dan.8.world_behind: Alexander's rapid conquest is matched exactly by the goat moving without touching the ground.

deep_background.note: The little horn's attack on the sanctuary and its evening offering fits the Maccabean crisis.

Dan.9.occasion: Daniel prays over Jeremiah's seventy years.
Dan.9.structure: Confession on behalf of the nation, then the seventy weeks and the anointed one.
Dan.9.world_behind: Reading Jeremiah's letter about seventy years prompted the prayer, tying the book to the exile's end.

deep_background.note: The weeks are counted in sevens of years, so the answer stretches far beyond the immediate return.

Dan.10.occasion: A vision beside the Tigris and the delayed answer.
Dan.10.structure: Three weeks of mourning, the glorious figure, the prince of Persia resisting, the messenger aided by Michael.
Dan.10.world_behind: Riverbank vision sites were standard in Near Eastern prophecy accounts, away from city crowds.

deep_background.note: Nations each have a heavenly prince, explaining why the answer came late despite prayer.

Dan.11.occasion: The long prophecy of north and south.
Dan.11.structure: Ptolemaic and Seleucid kings, the marriage and wars, the abomination, the persecuted faithful.
Dan.11.world_behind: Antiochus IV entered the temple and set up a pagan altar, the desecration the chapter clearly echoes.

deep_background.note: Even the faithful suffer in the crisis, so martyrdom becomes part of the book's answer.

Dan.12.occasion: The time of the end and the resurrection.
Dan.12.structure: Michael rises, the dead wake, the wise shine, then the sealed times and Daniel's rest.
Dan.12.world_behind: Persecution under Antiochus produced the first clear hope of bodily resurrection in Israel's writings.

deep_background.note: Sealing the words means the meaning is meant for the generation that lives through it.

Hos.1.occasion: Hosea is told to marry a promiscuous woman as a sign.
Hos.1.structure: The marriage, three children named for judgment, then a promise of restoration.
Hos.1.world_behind: Prophetic sign-acts made the message visible; a prophet's household became public text.

deep_background.note: Jezreel, Not-pitied and Not-my-people announce the covenant's reversal before the children can speak.

Hos.2.occasion: Israel's unfaithfulness is indicted as adultery.
Hos.2.structure: The charge, the hedge of thorns, the wilderness wooing, then betrothal in righteousness.
Hos.2.world_behind: Baal was appealed to for grain and wine, so Israel credited the land's fertility to a rival god.

deep_background.note: The marriage image moves from divorce to a new covenant, the book's central hope.

Hos.3.occasion: Hosea redeems his wife from slavery.
Hos.3.structure: Buy her back for silver and barley, then a long waiting before return.
Hos.3.world_behind: A slave's redemption price was paid in silver and grain, weighed rather than coined.

deep_background.note: Redemption here is a purchase, which is why the word carries both cost and rescue.

Hos.4.occasion: The LORD brings a lawsuit against the nation.
Hos.4.structure: No faithfulness in the land, the priests indicted, the people destroyed for lack of knowledge.
Hos.4.world_behind: Covenant lawsuits followed legal forms, with witnesses, charges and verdicts.

deep_background.note: The ignorance named is not information but refusal of relationship, so the priests bear the blame.

Hos.5.occasion: Judah and Israel are both warned of coming judgment.
Hos.5.structure: Leaders as a snare, Ephraim's sickness, the withdrawal until they seek him.
Hos.5.world_behind: Border disputes and shifting alliances with Assyria made both kingdoms unstable.

deep_background.note: God's absence is itself the judgment, which is why they will seek him and not find him.

Hos.6.occasion: A shallow repentance is answered with a call for mercy.
Hos.6.structure: The people's quick confession, then the charge of love like morning mist, then mercy over sacrifice.
Hos.6.world_behind: Rainy and dry seasons in Israel explain the mist image: it burns off by mid-morning.

deep_background.note: The Hebrew word hesed means covenant loyalty, and it is what the sacrifices were meant to express.

Hos.7.occasion: Israel's politics are described as a heated oven.
Hos.7.structure: Conspiracy, the oven of passion, foreign alliances, then the dove-like gullibility.
Hos.7.world_behind: Palace coups by assassination marked Israel's final decades, several kings dying within a year.

deep_background.note: Flatbread baked on coals must be turned; unbaked on one side means half-done devotion.

Hos.8.occasion: Israel claims to know God while breaking the covenant.
Hos.8.structure: They cry my God, then the calf of Samaria, the whirlwind sowing, forgotten Maker.
Hos.8.world_behind: Assyria absorbed vassal states that refused tribute, which is the wind the chapter names.

deep_background.note: The harvest image promises that a policy of deceit produces its own whirlwind.

Hos.9.occasion: Exile is announced for festival and harvest alike.
Hos.9.structure: No rejoicing, Egypt and Assyria as destinations, the prophet as a watchman hated.
Hos.9.world_behind: Exile meant unclean food and no temple, so the festivals themselves could not be kept.

deep_background.note: Gibeah's outrage is the book's touchstone for how far the nation had fallen before.

Hos.10.occasion: A luxuriant vine turned to idolatry is cut down.
Hos.10.structure: The vine and the empty altars, the calf carried to Assyria, then a call to sow righteousness.
Hos.10.world_behind: The high places were royal shrines, so removing them was a political act against the crown.

deep_background.note: Breaking up unploughed ground means the heart must be disrupted before good seed can root.

Hos.11.occasion: God's love for Ephraim is described as a parent's.
Hos.11.structure: Taught to walk, lifted and healed, then the refusal to give them up, then the lion's roar.
Hos.11.world_behind: Teaching a child to walk by holding the arms is a household picture of covenant care.

deep_background.note: God insists he is not a man, so his compassion does not turn with mood as human anger does.

Hos.12.occasion: Jacob's story is used to indict his descendants.
Hos.12.structure: Ephraim's lies, Jacob wrestling and weeping at Bethel, then a call to return.
Hos.12.world_behind: Jacob's shrine at Bethel was a northern sanctuary, so his story carried local weight.

deep_background.note: Remembering Jacob's struggle turns an ancestor's failure and prayer into a template for the nation.

Hos.13.occasion: Ephraim's idolatry is traced to its destruction.
Hos.13.structure: Exalted then forgotten, the wild beast and the leopard, then death's plagues reversed.
Hos.13.world_behind: The Assyrian deportations emptied the land of leadership and left wild animals unchecked.

deep_background.note: The taunt asks who will be king to save them now that kings were given in anger.

Hos.14.occasion: The book ends with an invitation to return.
Hos.14.structure: A call to bring words of repentance, then the dew and lily promises, then the closing wisdom line.
Hos.14.world_behind: Lily and olive imagery promise flourishing in a land where both were cultivated staples.

deep_background.concept: Ways of the LORD are right
deep_background.note: The book closes by saying the message is plain, and only the rebellious stumble on it.

Jol.1.occasion: A locust plague is treated as a national catastrophe.
Jol.1.structure: Successive locust swarms, ruined harvest, the priests told to wail, the day of the LORD near.
Jol.1.world_behind: Locust swarms strip everything, and the old men are called on because only they remember earlier ones.

deep_background.note: Public fasting was the standard response to crisis, gathering the whole community before God.

Jol.2.occasion: The army of locusts becomes the day of the LORD, then the Spirit is promised.
Jol.2.structure: Blow the trumpet, the army's advance, the call to rend hearts, restoration, then the outpoured Spirit.
Jol.2.world_behind: Ancient armies advanced like locust clouds, which is why the prophet slides between them.

deep_background.note: Tearing garments was external mourning; the command insists the tearing must happen inside.

Jol.3.occasion: The nations are judged in the valley and Zion is secured.
Jol.3.structure: Gather the nations for judgment at Jehoshaphat, then Judah's restoration and the LORD's dwelling in Zion.
Jol.3.world_behind: The Kidron valley below Jerusalem was a natural place for a judgment scene in the prophets.

deep_background.note: The word decision plays on Jehoshaphat's name, meaning the LORD judges.

Oba.1.occasion: Edom is judged for standing by during Jerusalem's fall.
Oba.1.structure: Edom's pride in its rock fortress, the charge of brotherly betrayal, then the LORD's reign on Zion.
Oba.1.world_behind: Edom's capital Petra sat in cliff-cut rock, so the pride of the heights was literal.

deep_background.note: Edom is Jacob's brother Esau, so the verdict turns on family betrayal, not foreign policy.

Jon.1.occasion: Jonah flees the call to Nineveh.
Jon.1.structure: The command, the flight by sea, the storm, the casting of lots, then the fish.
Jon.1.world_behind: Nineveh was Assyria's great city, the empire that would destroy Israel, so the mission was feared.

deep_background.note: Fleeing to the sea away from the land of Israel is fleeing toward what the ancient world called chaos.

Jon.2.occasion: Jonah's prayer from inside the fish.
Jon.2.structure: Cry from the deep, descent to the roots of the mountains, thanksgiving, then the fish delivers him.
Jon.2.world_behind: Hebrew psalm language of Sheol and the deep shapes the prayer, not a literal geography.

deep_background.note: Deliverance is deliberately unglamorous, which suits the book's tone toward its prophet.

Jon.3.structure: One sentence announced, then the king's decree, sackcloth for people and beasts, then God relents.
Jon.3.world_behind: Assyrian kings recorded such acts of humiliation in public to avert divine anger.

deep_background.note: The stated motive is that God is slow to anger, exactly what Jonah feared.

Jon.4.occasion: Jonah resents the mercy shown to Nineveh.
Jon.4.structure: The prophet's complaint, the leaf-plant, the worm, then the closing question from God.
Jon.4.world_behind: A shade plant over a booth was the only comfort on the edge of a thirsty summer city.

deep_background.note: The book ends with God's question, forcing the reader to answer for themselves.

Mic.1.occasion: The LORD is called as witness against Samaria and Jerusalem.
Mic.1.structure: The LORD descends, its effects on the mountains, Samaria demolished, the lament from Gath on.
Mic.1.world_behind: The chapter's wordplays on town names work only in Hebrew, turning place names into the very grief they will feel.

deep_background.note: The prophet's own undress becomes a sign of the coming deportation.

Mic.2.occasion: Land-grabbers are condemned and a remnant promised.
Mic.2.structure: Woe to those who seize fields, then the taunt song, then the promise of gathering.
Mic.2.world_behind: Family land was inalienable under the covenant, so seizing it broke both law and identity.

deep_background.note: A surveyor's line means restored boundaries, the exact reversal of the seized fields.

Mic.3.occasion: Judah's rulers, prophets and priests are indicted together.
Mic.3.structure: Leaders who eat the flesh of the people, prophets who sell verdicts, then Zion ploughed like a field.
Mic.3.world_behind: Prophets paid by results told kings what they wanted, which made the courts corrupt by design.

deep_background.note: The prediction that the temple hill becomes a field was cited a century later as still unfulfilled.

Mic.4.occasion: The mountain of the LORD and the coming peace.
Mic.4.structure: Nations stream to Zion, swords beaten into ploughshares, the LORD reigns, then exile and rescue.
Mic.4.world_behind: Iron ploughshares were repurposed swords in reverse, an image every farming household understood.

deep_background.note: The phrase means security and leisure, drawn from the peaceful end of a harvest.

Mic.5.occasion: A ruler will come from Bethlehem.
Mic.5.structure: The siege, the ruler from an insignificant clan, the remnant among the nations, then the purging of idols.
Mic.5.world_behind: Bethlehem was a small Judean town whose only fame was David's birth.

deep_background.note: The ruler's origin is pushed before human reckoning, which later tradition read messianically.

Mic.6.occasion: A covenant lawsuit sets out what the LORD requires.
Mic.6.structure: The LORD's case, the recital of mercies, the question of acceptable offering, then mercy, justice and humility.
Mic.6.world_behind: Courtroom forms structure the oracle: plaintiff, evidence, indictment and verdict.

deep_background.note: Escalating sacrifices expose the idea that God can be paid, which the answer rejects.

Mic.7.occasion: The book closes in lament, then confidence.
Mic.7.structure: No one upright remains, then watchfulness, then the LORD who delights in mercy and casts sins into the sea.
Mic.7.world_behind: Corruption of courts and households together meant no trustworthy institution was left.

deep_background.concept: Into the depths of the sea
deep_background.note: The image answers the exodus, making forgiveness the new crossing.

Nam.1.occasion: Nineveh is judged by the God who is slow to anger but not lenient.
Nam.1.structure: The LORD's character, the storm theophany, the stronghold, then the announcement against Assyria.
Nam.1.world_behind: Assyria was at its height, so announcing its fall was politically absurd when spoken.

deep_background.concept: Refuge in the day of trouble
deep_background.note: The same wrath that judges Assyria shelters those who take refuge in him.

Nam.2.occasion: The siege and fall of Nineveh depicted.
Nam.2.structure: The scatterer comes, shields reddened, the gates of the rivers opened, the palace dissolved, the lions' den plundered.
Nam.2.world_behind: Nineveh sat where the Khosr meets the Tigris, so river flooding really did breach its walls.

deep_background.note: Assyrian kings hunted and displayed lions, so the image of a den full of prey is a royal taunt.

Nam.3.structure: Woe, the chariots and corpses, the harlot's shame exposed, then the ruined fortress.
Nam.3.world_behind: Assyrian reliefs depicted impalement and flaying of captives, so the charge of blood is documented.

deep_background.note: Every ally who heard of the fall clapped, since Assyria's cruelty had touched them all.

Hab.1.occasion: The prophet protests violence and receives a shocking answer.
Hab.1.structure: Complaint about injustice, then the Chaldeans as God's instrument, then a second complaint.
Hab.1.world_behind: Babylon rose fast after 612 BC, so naming it as the coming power was a live threat.

deep_background.note: The verse quoted in the New Testament answers complaint with trust, not explanation.

Hab.2.occasion: The vision is written and the proud are indicted in five woes.
Hab.2.structure: Write the vision, the appointed time, five woe oracles, then silence before the LORD.
Hab.2.world_behind: Writing a vision on tablets meant public posting, so passers-by could read it.

deep_background.note: The promise answers idolatry: the knowledge of the LORD will cover the world like water.

Hab.3.occasion: A prayer-song of trust in the LORD's coming.
Hab.3.structure: Petition, the theophany from Teman, the shaking of nations, then joy despite ruin.
Hab.3.world_behind: Teman in Edom was famed for wisdom, so the LORD's march from the south is deliberate imagery.

deep_background.note: The vow to rejoice despite total crop loss is the book's answer to its own complaint.

Zep.1.occasion: The day of the LORD is announced against Judah and the nations.
Zep.1.structure: Sweeping judgment on land and city, the officials and the careless, then the great day described.
Zep.1.world_behind: Foreign dress and oaths by Milcom show how far court culture had absorbed other religions.

deep_background.note: God searching Jerusalem with lamps means nobody's private compromise stays hidden.

Zep.2.occasion: A call to seek the LORD before judgment falls on the nations.
Zep.2.structure: Seek humility, Philistia, Moab, Ammon, Cush and Assyria judged, then Nineveh desolate.
Zep.2.world_behind: Each nation named was a real neighbour State, so the oracle doubles as a map of threats.

deep_background.note: The first hopeful promise comes to the meek, not to the powerful or the religious elite.

Zep.3.occasion: Jerusalem's corruption, then the singing God.
Zep.3.structure: Woe to the city, the LORD's justice, the purged people, then the LORD rejoicing with singing.
Zep.3.world_behind: The city's officials are called roaring lions and evening wolves, imagery of predators in the streets.

deep_background.note: This is the only place in the Old Testament where God is said to sing over his people.

Hag.1.occasion: The people are rebuked for building their own houses while the temple lies waste.
Hag.1.structure: The date given, the indictment, the famine of harvests, then the stirring of the spirit.
Hag.1.world_behind: Rebuilding started 16 years late because Persia let local opposition stall the work.

deep_background.note: Panelling was royal luxury, so the charge is not necessity but misplaced priority.

Hag.2.occasion: The new temple is encouraged and the promise of shaking.
Hag.2.structure: The second temple's apparent smallness, the glory to come, the shaking of the nations, then Zerubbabel as signet.
Hag.2.world_behind: Old men wept comparing the modest second temple to Solomon's, which explains the encouragement.

deep_background.note: The phrasing is later applied to the unshakable kingdom in Hebrews.

Zec.1.occasion: Four night visions call Jerusalem back.
Zec.1.structure: A call to return, the horseman among the myrtles, the horns, the measuring line.
Zec.1.world_behind: Myrtle-growing valleys marked the Judaean hills, so the vision is set in familiar landscape.

deep_background.note: A man measuring the city promised rebuilding without walls, protection by God instead.

Zec.2.occasion: The city's expansion and the LORD's dwelling among them.
Zec.2.structure: Measuring the city, the call for exiles to return, the promise that many nations will join.
Zec.2.world_behind: A walled city's size was fixed by its walls, so 'without walls' means uncounted population.

deep_background.note: The image is of a pupil, the part of the eye that cannot be touched without blinding the person.

Zec.3.occasion: Joshua the high priest is cleansed in a courtroom scene.
Zec.3.structure: Satan accusing, filthy garments replaced, the promise of the Branch, the stone.
Zec.3.world_behind: The high priest's garments were part of the office, so changing clothes meant changing standing.

deep_background.note: Feces-soiled clothing was the extremity of ritual uncleanness, so the gift is not small.

Zec.4.occasion: The lampstand and the two olive trees.
Zec.4.structure: The lampstand vision, the question answered, then not by might but by the Spirit, then the two anointed ones.
Zec.4.world_behind: The temple lampstand burned olive oil, so trees feeding a lamp directly is a deliberate impossibility.

deep_background.note: The verse answers a small, unarmed community facing a province's opposition.

Zec.5.occasion: Two visions remove sin and wickedness from the land.
Zec.5.structure: A flying scroll of curses, then a basket with a woman named Wickedness carried to Shinar.
Zec.5.world_behind: An ephah basket was a standard grain measure, and lead sealed its contents.

deep_background.note: Sin is carried out of the land to Babylon, reversing the exile's direction.

Zec.6.occasion: Four chariots and the crowning of the Branch.
Zec.6.structure: Chariots from between bronze mountains, the crowning of Joshua, then the Branch who builds the temple.
Zec.6.world_behind: Crowns were kept in the temple as votive deposits, so the sign remained visible afterward.

deep_background.note: Priest and king are joined in one figure, a fusion Israel had deliberately kept apart.

Zec.7.occasion: A question about fasting gets a moral answer.
Zec.7.structure: Envoys ask about the fast of the fifth month, then the answer about justice and the wilderness years.
Zec.7.world_behind: Memorial fasts marked the temple's destruction, so the question was about grief and its end.

deep_background.note: Ritual grief that ignores the widow and orphan is exposed as self-directed religion.

Zec.8.occasion: Zion restored with old and young in the streets.
Zec.8.structure: Ten promises of restoration, then the fasts turned to feasts, then nations seeking the LORD.
Zec.8.world_behind: Old men and children in the squares is a picture of a city safe enough to be leisurely.

deep_background.note: The reversal is complete when foreigners take hold of a Jew's robe to go with him.

Zec.9.occasion: The king comes to Zion riding a donkey.
Zec.9.structure: Judgment on the coastal cities, then the humble king, then the LORD's defence of his people.
Zec.9.world_behind: A donkey was a royal mount for peace; horses meant war, which is why the image matters.

deep_background.note: The verse is quoted directly at the triumphal entry, making the animal the point.

Zec.10.occasion: The LORD gathers the scattered flock.
Zec.10.structure: Teraphim and diviners rebuked, then the shepherding of Judah and Ephraim, then their strength.
Zec.10.world_behind: Household idols called teraphim were consulted for guidance, often alongside the LORD.

deep_background.note: The image of a cornerstone, tent peg and battle bow gathers leadership pictures into one promise.

Zec.11.occasion: The shepherd rejected and the flock broken.
Zec.11.structure: The cedar's fall, two staffs named Favour and Union, the thirty pieces of silver, the worthless shepherd.
Zec.11.world_behind: Thirty shekels was the compensation price for a gored slave, a deliberate insult here.

deep_background.note: The prophet acts out God's own grief at being rejected by the flock he fed.

Zec.12.occasion: Jerusalem a cup of trembling, and mourning over the pierced one.
Zec.12.structure: Siege defeated, the inhabitants strengthened, then the spirit of grace and mourning for the pierced.
Zec.12.world_behind: Mourning like Hadad-rimmon refers to a public lament for a slain king in the Jezreel valley.

deep_background.note: The verse is quoted in John's passion account as fulfilled at the cross.

Zec.13.occasion: Cleansing from sin and the shepherd struck.
Zec.13.structure: A fountain opened, idols and prophets cut off, then the shepherd struck and the sheep scattered.
Zec.13.world_behind: False prophets would deny the calling to avoid the suspicion attached to prophecy after the exile.

deep_background.note: Jesus cites the striking of the shepherd when predicting the disciples' scattering.

Zec.14.occasion: The day of the LORD and the renewed city.
Zec.14.structure: Nations gathered, the mount split, the LORD reigns, then the pilgrimage of the nations and the plague.
Zec.14.world_behind: The Mount of Olives sits east of the city, so a split there reads as a new escape route.

deep_background.note: Water flowing east and west means both seas are healed, the same image as Ezekiel's river.

Mal.1.occasion: The LORD's love for Jacob is asserted against a doubting people.
Mal.1.structure: I have loved you, then Esau's rejection, then the defiled offerings and the worthless animals.
Mal.1.world_behind: Blemished animals were cheap, so the priests were profiting by selling the good ones and offering the rest.

deep_background.note: The charge is that their worship insulted the very name they claimed to honour.

Mal.2.occasion: The priests' covenant and the people's unfaithfulness.
Mal.2.structure: Priests rebuked, the levitical covenant recalled, then the charge against marriage to foreign gods.
Mal.2.world_behind: Intermarriage dissolved land and religious loyalty and was a live issue after the exile, as Ezra shows.

deep_background.note: The promised messenger refines the priests, so purification begins inside the temple.

Mal.3.occasion: The messenger comes and the LORD's justice is defended.
Mal.3.structure: The messenger and the refiner, then tithes withheld and the day of the returning Elijah.
Mal.3.world_behind: Tithe grain stored in the temple fed the priests and the poor, so withholding it starved both.

deep_background.note: A written record of those who feared the LORD answers the claim that serving him is useless.

Mal.4.occasion: The day burns and the prophet Elijah returns.
Mal.4.structure: The day as a furnace and as healing sun, then the command to remember Moses and the promise of Elijah.
Mal.4.world_behind: An unfulfilled Elijah promise kept hope open across centuries, which is why the New Testament opens with it.

deep_background.note: The same sun that burns the proud heals the faithful, one fire with two effects.

Amo.1.occasion: The LORD roars from Zion and indicts the nations.
Amo.1.structure: Eight oracles begin: Damascus, Gaza, Tyre, Edom, Ammon, Moab, each for a named crime.
Amo.1.world_behind: Treaties and border raids were routine, so naming specific atrocities is unusually precise.

deep_background.note: The formula means the cup is full, not that the count is exact.

Amo.2.occasion: Judah and Israel are indicted after the nations.
Amo.2.structure: Moab, then Judah for rejecting the law, then Israel for selling the righteous for silver.
Amo.2.world_behind: Selling a poor man for a pair of sandals means debt slavery over trivial sums.

deep_background.note: Israel is charged with blocking the very people God raised up to call it back.

Amo.3.occasion: The lion has roared, so who can but prophesy?
Amo.3.structure: Cause and effect arguments, then the charge of oppression in Samaria, then the altar horns cut off.
Amo.3.world_behind: Horned altars offered asylum; cutting the horns removed the last refuge for the accused.

deep_background.note: Election is turned into greater accountability, not exemption.

Amo.4.occasion: Wealthy women and empty worship are condemned.
Amo.4.structure: Cows of Bashan, then the catalogue of disasters that failed to turn them, then prepare to meet your God.
Amo.4.world_behind: Bashan's cattle were proverbial for fatness, and the image targets the wealthy of Samaria.

deep_background.note: The covenant curses of Leviticus 26 are recounted as already happened, not threatened.

Amo.5.occasion: A funeral song over Israel, then the call for justice.
Amo.5.structure: Dirge, seek the LORD and live, woe to the complacent, then let justice roll down like waters.
Amo.5.world_behind: Bethel and Gilgal were royal shrines, so the command not to seek them was a rejection of state religion.

deep_background.note: The prophet is the first to say the people's hoped-for day will be darkness for them.

Amo.6.occasion: Woe to those at ease in Zion and Samaria.
Amo.6.structure: Beds of ivory, wine and music, then the exile announced, then the ruin of the house.
Amo.6.world_behind: Ivory-inlaid furniture is attested in Samaria's palace excavations.

deep_background.note: The charge is indifference to a collapsing nation while enjoying its wealth.

Amo.7.occasion: Three visions and a confrontation with the priest.
Amo.7.structure: Locusts, fire, plumb line, then Amaziah's accusation and Amos's reply.
Amo.7.world_behind: The king's sanctuary at Bethel made the priest a royal official, so the clash was political.

deep_background.note: A wall measured and found crooked explains why intercession is refused at this point.

Amo.8.occasion: The basket of summer fruit marks the end.
Amo.8.structure: Ripe fruit, then greed and dishonest scales, then the famine of hearing the word of the LORD.
Amo.8.world_behind: False ephahs and rigged balances are documented in ancient market practice.

deep_background.note: The worst judgment is silence, when people search for a word and none comes.

Amo.9.occasion: The LORD at the altar, then the restored booth of David.
Amo.9.structure: No escape from judgment, the altar struck, then the fallen booth raised and the land restored.
Amo.9.world_behind: A booth is a temporary shelter, so David's fallen dynasty is pictured as a collapsed hut.

deep_background.note: The promise is quoted at the Jerusalem council in Acts as grounds for including the nations.

Mat.1.occasion: Genealogy, virgin birth, and the Magi arrive in Bethlehem.
Mat.1.structure: Legal genealogy from Abraham, Joseph's dream, the visit of the Magi, the flight to Egypt, and the return to Nazareth.
Mat.1.world_behind: Matthew opens on a Jewish audience, tracing the line to Abraham and David to prove the Messiah's legal claim.

deep_background.note: Eastern astrologer-priests read the sky for royal births, and their gifts fit a king.

Mat.2.occasion: Herod's slaughter and the flight to Egypt.
Mat.2.structure: Magi warned in a dream, flight to Egypt, the killing of the infants, and the return to Nazareth.
Mat.2.world_behind: Herod the Great was ruthless about rivals, and Bethlehem lay within his reach, so the violence fits his record.

deep_background.note: The verse quotes Jeremiah's Ramah lament, tying the massacre to Israel's exile grief.

Mat.3.occasion: John the Baptist prepares the way and baptizes Jesus.
Mat.3.structure: John's preaching, the Pharisees rebuked, the baptism, the Spirit descending, the Father's voice.
Mat.3.world_behind: Baptism by immersion in the Jordan was a rite for converts, so John's call to Israel was provocative.

deep_background.note: Crossing the Jordan meant entering the land, so baptism there carried a new-exodus meaning.

Mat.4.occasion: Temptation in the wilderness and the first disciples called.
Mat.4.structure: Three temptations, withdrawal to Galilee, calling of four fishermen, and a healing tour.
Mat.4.world_behind: The Spirit drives Jesus into Judean desert country, where forty days of fasting echoes Israel's forty years.

deep_background.note: Forty days echoes Israel's forty years of testing and Moses' forty days on the mountain.

Mat.5.occasion: The Sermon on the Mount opens with the beatitudes.
Mat.5.structure: Beatitudes, salt and light, the law interpreted, anger, lust, oaths, and love of enemies.
Mat.5.world_behind: Teaching on a hillside was ordinary for Galilean teachers, who sat to teach and taught in memorable patterns.

deep_background.note: Blessing language in the Old Testament named God's favor, not merely a happy mood.

Mat.6.occasion: True piety, the Lord's Prayer, and trust in God.
Mat.6.structure: Almsgiving, prayer, fasting, the Lord's Prayer, treasures in heaven, and anxiety about provision.
Mat.6.world_behind: Public giving and loud prayer were visible social performances in village life, so private practice was a real contrast.

deep_background.note: Mammon means wealth treated as a rival master, not just money itself.

Mat.7.occasion: Judging, prayer, and the narrow gate close the sermon.
Mat.7.structure: Do not judge, ask and receive, the golden rule, the two gates, false prophets, and the house on rock.
Mat.7.world_behind: The sermon ends with a building image his hearers knew, since Galilean houses stood on bedrock or sand.

deep_background.note: City gates were narrow enough to control traffic, so the image meant a deliberate choice.

Mat.8.occasion: Authority displayed over disease, distance, and storm.
Mat.8.structure: Leper cleansed, centurion's servant healed, Peter's mother-in-law, the storm stilled, and two demoniacs freed.
Mat.8.world_behind: A centurion commanded about eighty soldiers, and his appeal on behalf of a slave was socially unusual.

deep_background.note: Rock-cut tombs outside a town were considered unclean and were associated with the demonic.

Mat.9.structure: Paralytic forgiven and healed, Matthew called, fasting questioned, two women healed, and the crowds likened to a harvest.
Mat.9.world_behind: Tax collectors worked for Rome and were shunned, so dining with them was a public scandal.

deep_background.note: The tassels on a Jewish man's cloak marked covenant loyalty, so touching them was a plea for mercy.

Mat.10.structure: Twelve named and sent, instructions for the road, persecution foretold, and the cost of discipleship.
Mat.10.world_behind: Traveling teachers depended on hospitality, so the instructions about lodging reflect real practice.

deep_background.note: Shaking dust from the feet was a gesture of disassociation, treating a town as outside Israel.

Mat.11.occasion: John's question from prison and woe to the unrepentant towns.
Mat.11.structure: John's messengers, Jesus' testimony about John, woe to Chorazin and Bethsaida, and the invitation to the weary.
Mat.11.world_behind: Herod Antipas held John in the fortress at Machaerus, so the question came from a man awaiting execution.

deep_background.note: A rabbi's yoke meant his teaching, so a light yoke meant a bearable way of life.

Mat.12.occasion: Sabbath conflict and the sign of Jonah.
Mat.12.structure: Grainfield and hand controversies, Beelzebub accusation, the unforgivable sin, the sign of Jonah, and true family.
Mat.12.world_behind: Sabbath law debate was live in the first century, and healing was classed as work by some schools.

deep_background.note: Jonah spent three days in the fish, which the Gospel reads as a pattern for burial and return.

Mat.13.occasion: The parable discourse by the lake.
Mat.13.structure: Sower, weeds among wheat, mustard seed, leaven, hidden treasure, pearl, and the net, then rejection at Nazareth.
Mat.13.world_behind: Farming on the Galilean plain used broadcast sowing, so seed falling on paths and rock was ordinary experience.

deep_background.note: Leaven usually pictured corruption in Jewish teaching, so using it for the kingdom reverses expectation.

Mat.14.occasion: John beheaded and the five thousand fed.
Mat.14.structure: Herod's banquet and John's death, withdrawal to a lonely place, feeding of five thousand, and walking on the sea.
Mat.14.world_behind: Herod's birthday banquet with a rash oath fits the court culture of a client king answerable to Rome.

deep_background.note: A wilderness setting echoes Israel fed in the desert, framing the meal as new provision.

Mat.15.occasion: Tradition, a Canaanite woman, and a second feeding.
Mat.15.structure: Handwashing dispute, the woman's persistent plea, healings by the lake, and four thousand fed.
Mat.15.world_behind: Ritual handwashing was a marker of purity practiced strictly by some groups and not by others.

deep_background.note: Household dogs were pets, not street animals, which softens the image into a promise of crumbs.

Mat.16.occasion: Peter's confession and the first passion prediction.
Mat.16.structure: A sign demanded, the leaven warning, confession at Caesarea Philippi, and the rebuke of Peter.
Mat.16.world_behind: Caesarea Philippi sat at a pagan shrine, making the confession land against a backdrop of rival gods.

deep_background.note: Keys meant authority to open and shut, an image drawn from the steward of a household.

Mat.17.occasion: The transfiguration on a high mountain.
Mat.17.structure: Glory revealed with Moses and Elijah, the boy with a seizure healed, and the temple tax paid from a fish.
Mat.17.world_behind: High mountains were places of revelation in Jewish memory, and Moses and Elijah were expected to return.

deep_background.note: Every adult male paid the half-shekel for the temple, so the question tested Jesus' standing.

Mat.18.structure: A child in their midst, causing stumbling, the lost sheep, restoring a brother, and seventy times seven.
Mat.18.world_behind: Children had no status, so placing a child as the model overturned the honor ranking of the day.

deep_background.note: The number answers a rabbinic limit of three forgivenesses, exceeding even a generous reading.

Mat.19.occasion: Teaching on divorce and the rich young man.
Mat.19.structure: Marriage and divorce, children welcomed, the rich man's refusal, and the reward of the disciples.
Mat.19.world_behind: Divorce was a legal dispute between schools, and a father's property interests shaped how passage was discussed.

deep_background.note: Some readers propose a needle gate, but the image is meant as deliberate impossibility with men.

Mat.20.occasion: Grace equal in the vineyard and the last passion prediction.
Mat.20.structure: Laborers hired at every hour, James and John's request, and two blind men healed at Jericho.
Mat.20.world_behind: Day laborers gathered at dawn in the market square, and a denarius was one day's wage.

deep_background.note: Honor culture ranked seating at a host's table, so servanthood as greatness was a direct inversion.

Mat.21.occasion: Entry into Jerusalem and the temple confrontation.
Mat.21.structure: Triumphal entry, fig tree cursed, temple cleansed, and the parable of the tenants.
Mat.21.world_behind: Pilgrim crowds came to Jerusalem for Passover under Roman guard, so any procession was politically loaded.

deep_background.note: A tree in leaf before season suggests false promise, an acted parable beside the temple action.

Mat.22.structure: Wedding banquet parable, tribute to Caesar, the resurrection question, and the greatest commandment.
Mat.22.world_behind: Coins carried Caesar's image, and Roman taxation was a daily irritant carrying political weight.

deep_background.note: The temple tax was paid in the Tyrian standard, which explains the demand for the coin.

Mat.23.occasion: The seven woes against the scribes and Pharisees.
Mat.23.structure: The crowds warned, seven woes pronounced, and a lament over Jerusalem.
Mat.23.world_behind: Pharisees were lay reformers who took purity seriously, and their influence was significant in towns.

deep_background.note: Whitewashed tombs were marked to prevent defilement, so the image means subtle uncleanness.

Mat.24.occasion: The Olivet discourse on the end of the age.
Mat.24.structure: The temple's fall predicted, signs and distress, the coming of the Son of Man, and a fig tree lesson.
Mat.24.world_behind: The temple's stones were enormous, so predicting its collapse was politically dangerous in the day.

deep_background.note: The term refers to the desecration spoken of by Daniel, which readers have applied to several events.

Mat.25.structure: Ten virgins, the talents, and the sheep and goats.
Mat.25.world_behind: Wedding processions waited for the groom at night, so lamps and oil were practical necessities.

deep_background.note: A talent was a weight of silver worth many years of wages, so the sums are enormous.

Mat.26.occasion: The passion begins: supper, arrest, and trial.
Mat.26.structure: Plot and anointing, last supper, Gethsemane, arrest, trials before Caiaphas, and Peter's denial.
Mat.26.world_behind: Passover pilgrims crowded Jerusalem, and the Roman prefect came up from Caesarea for the feast.

deep_background.note: The sum matches the price of a slave in Exodus, marking the betrayal as an insult.

Mat.27.structure: Pilate and the crowd, scourging, crucifixion, the cry of dereliction, the temple curtain, and the guarded tomb.
Mat.27.world_behind: Roman crucifixion was reserved for rebels and slaves, and the body was normally left unburied.

deep_background.note: The inner curtain screened the holiest place, so tearing it signalled unrestricted access to God.

Mat.28.structure: The empty tomb, the guards' report, the appearance in Galilee, and the sending of the eleven.
Mat.28.world_behind: A Roman guard unit posted at a tomb carried liability for losing a body, which explains the bribe.

deep_background.note: The command reaches all nations, extending a message that began with Israel alone.

Mrk.1.occasion: John prepares, Jesus is baptized, and the Galilean ministry begins.
Mrk.1.structure: John's preaching, baptism and temptation, four disciples called, a Capernaum sabbath, and a leper cleansed.
Mrk.1.world_behind: Capernaum sat on the lake's trade route, so a synagogue, a customs post, and fishing work all stood within sight.

deep_background.note: Mark's favourite word drives the pace, presenting the ministry as urgent and compact.

Mrk.2.occasion: Forgiveness, calling, and the first sabbath disputes.
Mrk.2.structure: Paralytic lowered through the roof, Levi called, fasting questioned, and grain picked on the sabbath.
Mrk.2.world_behind: A mud and thatch roof could be dug open, which is exactly how the friends reached the room.

deep_background.note: Wineskins were animal skins that cracked when old, so new wine required fresh skins.

Mrk.3.occasion: A healing on the sabbath and the twelve appointed.
Mrk.3.structure: Withered hand restored, crowds by the lake, the twelve named, the Beelzebub charge, and true family defined.
Mrk.3.world_behind: Herodians were supporters of the ruling house, and their alliance with Pharisees shows shared alarm.

deep_background.note: The warning is about attributing God's own work to an unclean spirit, not about any single slip.

Mrk.4.occasion: Parables by the lake and the storm stilled.
Mrk.4.structure: Sower, lamp under a basket, growing seed, mustard seed, and the calming of the sea.
Mrk.4.world_behind: Boats on the lake were small and open, so sudden Galilee squalls were genuinely dangerous.

deep_background.note: Cold air off the surrounding hills funnels onto the water, producing violent sudden winds.

Mrk.5.occasion: A demoniac freed, a daughter raised, a woman healed.
Mrk.5.structure: Gerasene tombs, the herd of pigs, Jairus' plea, the bleeding woman, and the girl raised.
Mrk.5.world_behind: Pig herding near a Gentile region tells you the economy and population there were not observant Jewish.

deep_background.note: A legion was a Roman army unit of thousands, used here as a name for the many spirits.

Mrk.6.occasion: Nazareth rejects him, John dies, and five thousand eat.
Mrk.6.structure: Rejection at Nazareth, the twelve sent out, Herod's banquet and John's death, the five thousand fed, and walking on the water.
Mrk.6.world_behind: Herod Antipas ruled Galilee, and his banquet with a tetrarch's court fits the politics of the region.

deep_background.note: Mark alone notes the grass, which points to spring and the Passover season.

Mrk.7.occasion: Tradition questioned and a Gentile woman answered.
Mrk.7.structure: Handwashing dispute, the Syrophoenician woman, and a deaf man healed in the Decapolis.
Mrk.7.world_behind: The Decapolis was a Greek-speaking region east of the lake, which explains the crowd's response to a Gentile mission.

deep_background.note: Corban meant a gift dedicated to God, which some used to avoid supporting parents.

Mrk.8.occasion: Four thousand fed and Peter confesses.
Mrk.8.structure: Second feeding, the leaven warning, a blind man healed in stages, and the confession at Caesarea Philippi.
Mrk.8.world_behind: Caesarea Philippi stood near a spring sacred to Pan, so the confession lands beside pagan worship.

deep_background.note: The gradual healing is unique to Mark and stresses that sight came slowly to the disciples too.

Mrk.9.structure: Glory on the mountain, the boy with a spirit, the argument about greatness, and warnings about stumbling.
Mrk.9.world_behind: A father's cry about unbelief reflects the ordinary desperation of a family with an afflicted child.

deep_background.note: Salt preserved and seasoned, so the image calls for a distinctive, useful life.

Mrk.10.occasion: Teaching on marriage, wealth, and service.
Mrk.10.structure: Divorce, children blessed, the rich man, James and John's request, and Bartimaeus healed.
Mrk.10.world_behind: Jericho sat on the pilgrim road to Jerusalem, which is why a blind beggar would be positioned there.

deep_background.note: The image is deliberately impossible, making wealth's obstacle a matter of God's action.

Mrk.11.occasion: Entry into Jerusalem and the temple cleansed.
Mrk.11.structure: Triumphal entry, fig tree cursed, temple cleared, and the authority question.
Mrk.11.world_behind: The temple court hosted merchants and money changers for pilgrims, making the trade necessary and profitable.

deep_background.note: An unridden animal was suitable for sacred use, which fits the deliberate symbolism.

Mrk.12.occasion: Temple controversy and a widow's gift.
Mrk.12.structure: Tenants parable, tribute to Caesar, resurrection question, greatest commandment, and the widow's two coins.
Mrk.12.world_behind: The treasury stood in the women's court, where gifts were given publicly and audibly.

deep_background.note: Roman coinage and temple coinage were different currencies, which frames the tribute question.

Mrk.13.occasion: The Olivet discourse on the temple's fall and the end.
Mrk.13.structure: Temple stones foretold, birth pangs, persecution, the abomination, the coming, and the fig tree lesson.
Mrk.13.world_behind: Herod's temple was one of the largest construction projects of the era, still unfinished in Jesus' day.

deep_background.note: The Roman siege and fire left the temple dismantled, which later readers took as confirmation.

Mrk.14.occasion: Anointing, last supper, arrest, and denial.
Mrk.14.structure: Bethany anointing, Passover meal, Gethsemane, arrest, night trial, and Peter's three denials.
Mrk.14.world_behind: Passover required a lamb and unleavened bread, and Jerusalem swelled with pilgrims for the feast.

deep_background.note: Abba is an intimate family address for father, unusual in prayer language of the period.

Mrk.15.occasion: Trial before Pilate, crucifixion, and burial.
Mrk.15.structure: Pilate and Barabbas, mockery, crucifixion, the cry of dereliction, the curtain torn, and Joseph's tomb.
Mrk.15.world_behind: Pilate governed Judaea directly and was known for harsh responses to unrest, which fits the crowd scene.

deep_background.note: Roman flogging used bone and metal in the lash and often preceded crucifixion, weakening the victim first.

Mrk.16.occasion: The empty tomb and the resurrection appearances.
Mrk.16.structure: Women at the tomb, the young man's announcement, the longer ending with appearances and commission.
Mrk.16.world_behind: A stone rolled across a tomb entrance was heavy, and a Roman seal or guard made tampering risky.

deep_background.note: Manuscript evidence varies here, which is why some Bibles mark the final verses as a later addition.

Luk.1.occasion: Luke's prologue and the births of John and Jesus foretold.
Luk.1.structure: Dedication to Theophilus, Zechariah's temple vision, Mary's visit, the Magnificat, and John's birth.
Luk.1.world_behind: Temple incense service fell by lot, and a priest served one annual rotation, so Zechariah's turn was rare.

deep_background.note: Mary's song quotes Hannah's prayer, casting the birth in the pattern of Israel's deliverance.

Luk.2.occasion: The birth of Jesus, the shepherds, and the boy in the temple.
Luk.2.structure: Census and manger, angelic announcement, presentation, Simeon and Anna, then Jesus at twelve.
Luk.2.world_behind: A Roman census required travel to a family's ancestral town, which explains the Bethlehem journey.

deep_background.note: A feeding trough signalled a birth in the crowded animal space of a village home, not an inn rejection.

Luk.3.occasion: John's preaching, Jesus' baptism, and the genealogy.
Luk.3.structure: Preaching of repentance, baptism, the descent of the Spirit, and a genealogy reaching Adam.
Luk.3.world_behind: Baptism in the Jordan was public, and crowds came from Judaea and beyond the river.

deep_background.note: Luke traces the line through Adam rather than Abraham, framing the mission for all nations.

Luk.4.structure: Wilderness testing, Isaiah read at Nazareth, rejection by the town, then Capernaum healings.
Luk.4.world_behind: Nazareth was a small hill village, and a visiting teacher read standing and sat to explain.

deep_background.note: The release and good news of Isaiah 61 carry the social shape of the Jubilee year.

Luk.5.occasion: Calls to discipleship and healings in Capernaum.
Luk.5.structure: Peter's catch, the leper, the paralytic through the roof, and Levi's feast.
Luk.5.world_behind: Fishing on Galilee used nets and boats at night, and the catch was sold fresh the same day.

deep_background.note: Houses had flat mud roofs reached by outside stairs, so digging through one was possible.

Luk.6.occasion: Sabbath conflicts, the twelve chosen, and the sermon on the plain.
Luk.6.structure: Grain and hand healings, the naming of the twelve, then blessings and woes.
Luk.6.world_behind: Pharisee sabbath rules aimed at protecting the day, so food plucking posed a live legal question.

deep_background.note: Luke sets the teaching on level ground after a night of prayer, unlike Matthew's mountain.

Luk.7.occasion: Faith outside Israel and mercy to the dead and the sinful.
Luk.7.structure: Centurion's servant, widow's son raised at Nain, John's question, and the sinful woman anointed Jesus' feet.
Luk.7.world_behind: A centurion commanded roughly a hundred soldiers and often funded a local synagogue.

deep_background.note: Nain sat near Nazareth, and a funeral procession met Jesus at the town gate.

Luk.8.occasion: Parables of the kingdom and power over storm, demons, and death.
Luk.8.structure: Sower explained, storm stilled, Gerasene deliverance, Jairus' daughter, and the bleeding woman.
Luk.8.world_behind: Gennesaret boats were small and open, so a sudden squall could swamp them quickly.

deep_background.note: A legion named a Roman unit of thousands, a deliberate image of occupying power in one man.

Luk.9.occasion: The twelve sent, the five thousand fed, and the transfiguration.
Luk.9.structure: Mission charge, Herod's confusion, the feeding, Peter's confession, glory on the mountain, and the boy healed.
Luk.9.world_behind: Herod Antipas ruled Galilee and had executed John, so reports of Jesus reached him directly.

deep_background.note: Moses and Elijah speak of a departure, tying the journey to Jerusalem to the exodus pattern.

Luk.10.occasion: The seventy-two sent out, and the good Samaritan.
Luk.10.structure: Mission of the seventy-two, their return, the lawyer's question, the Samaritan parable, and Mary and Martha.
Luk.10.world_behind: The Jericho road dropped steeply through rocky ground, notorious for robbery.

deep_background.note: Samaritans shared the Torah but worshipped on Gerizim, so the choice of hero was pointed.

Luk.11.occasion: Teaching on prayer and the sign of Jonah.
Luk.11.structure: Lord's Prayer, friend at midnight, persistent asking, Beelzebub accusation, and woes to the Pharisees.
Luk.11.world_behind: Hospitality required feeding a night guest, so the reluctant friend's refusal broke social obligation.

deep_background.note: Jonah preached to a foreign city, so the sign anticipates judgment reversed for outsiders.

Luk.12.occasion: Warnings about hypocrisy, greed, and anxiety.
Luk.12.structure: Leaven of the Pharisees, fear God, the rich fool, care for the sparrows, and readiness for the master.
Luk.12.world_behind: Barns were stone or mud storerooms, and a bumper harvest meant building bigger ones.

deep_background.note: The parable's farmer speaks only to himself, which is the point of the portrait.

Luk.13.occasion: Calls to repentance and the narrow door.
Luk.13.structure: Galilean deaths, the barren fig tree, the bent woman healed, mustard seed and leaven, and the lament over Jerusalem.
Luk.13.world_behind: A tower at Siloam collapsed, and Pilate had killed worshippers, both fresh news to the crowd.

deep_background.note: Long illness had no healing in Israel's practice, so the sabbath healing was disputed not denied.

Luk.14.occasion: Table teaching on humility and the cost of discipleship.
Luk.14.structure: Dropsy healed, seats at the feast, the great banquet, and counting the cost.
Luk.14.world_behind: Banquets seated guests by rank, and host and guest were bound by reciprocal obligation.

deep_background.note: Building a tower meant hiring labor and buying stone, so the planning image was concrete.

Luk.15.occasion: Three parables of the lost answered to grumbling.
Luk.15.structure: Lost sheep, lost coin, and the prodigal son with the elder brother.
Luk.15.world_behind: A shepherd left a flock in open country, and a village woman's ten coins were likely a headdress.

deep_background.note: Restoring robe, ring and sandals reinstated the son as a family member, not a servant.

Luk.16.occasion: Teaching on wealth and the rich man and Lazarus.
Luk.16.structure: The shrewd manager, faithful use of money, and the reversal of rich man and beggar.
Luk.16.world_behind: Managers handled another's estate and could reduce debts by cutting their own commission.

deep_background.note: Reclining beside Abraham at the feast pictured the place of honour in the world to come.

Luk.17.occasion: Faith, duty, gratitude, and the coming of the kingdom.
Luk.17.structure: Stumbling and forgiveness, the mustard seed, the servant's duty, ten lepers, and the kingdom's arrival.
Luk.17.world_behind: Lepers kept distance and had to show themselves to priests for readmission to the community.

deep_background.note: Only the foreigner returned, and the silence of the others is the shock of the story.

Luk.18.occasion: Persistent prayer and the cost of following.
Luk.18.structure: The widow and the judge, Pharisee and tax collector, children welcomed, the rich ruler, and blind Bartimaeus.
Luk.18.world_behind: Jericho sat on the trade road, so a blind beggar there met constant traffic and alms.

deep_background.note: The tax collector goes home declared righteous, the reversal on which the parable turns.

Luk.19.occasion: Zacchaeus, the minas, and the entry into Jerusalem.
Luk.19.structure: Zacchaeus converted, the ten minas, the colt and the crowd, and the lament over the city.
Luk.19.world_behind: A chief tax collector contracted for revenue and grew rich on the margin above the bid.

deep_background.note: The fig-mulberry tree had low spreading branches, easy to climb and see over a crowd.

Luk.20.occasion: Controversies in the temple courts during the final week.
Luk.20.structure: Authority questioned, the tenants, tribute to Caesar, the resurrection riddle, and David's son.
Luk.20.world_behind: The temple courts were the public teaching space, and the authorities held the licensing there.

deep_background.note: The coin bore Caesar's image, so the question trapped Jesus between revolt and collaboration.

Luk.21.occasion: The widow's gift and the Olivet discourse.
Luk.21.structure: Two copper coins, the temple's ruin foretold, persecution, Jerusalem encircled, and the call to watch.
Luk.21.world_behind: Temple treasury boxes received gifts publicly, so the widow's offering was visible to onlookers.

deep_background.note: Two lepta were the smallest copper coins, worth a fraction of a day's wage.

Luk.22.occasion: The last supper, arrest, and trials.
Luk.22.structure: Judas' bargain, the supper and the cup, Gethsemane, arrest, trials, and Peter's denial.
Luk.22.world_behind: Passover required unleavened bread and a lamb, eaten in the city after nightfall.

deep_background.note: At the table the dispute over rank inverts the household hierarchy the disciples expected.

Luk.23.occasion: Trial before Pilate, crucifixion, and burial.
Luk.23.structure: Accusations and Herod, Barabbas, the way to the cross, the two criminals, the death, and the tomb.
Luk.23.world_behind: Pilate sent a Galilean defendant to Herod Antipas as a courtesy during the feast.

deep_background.note: The promise to the criminal uses a garden word, answering the request to be remembered.

Luk.24.structure: Women at the tomb, the walk to Emmaus, the appearance to the eleven, and the departure near Bethany.
Luk.24.world_behind: Emmaus lay about seven miles from Jerusalem, a walk of roughly two hours.

deep_background.note: Recognition comes at the table, which became the pattern the early church repeated.

Jhn.1.occasion: The Word made flesh and the first disciples called.
Jhn.1.structure: Prologue hymn, the Baptist's testimony, the Lamb of God, and the calling of Andrew, Peter, Philip and Nathanael.
Jhn.1.world_behind: Bethany beyond the Jordan was a baptism site where crowds gathered to hear John.

deep_background.note: The opening echoes both Genesis creation speech and Greek thought about ordering reason.

Jhn.2.occasion: The first sign at Cana and the temple cleansing.
Jhn.2.structure: Water into wine at a wedding, then the Passover visit and the clearing of the courts.
Jhn.2.world_behind: Stone jars for purification held water for ritual washing, dozens of gallons at a time.

deep_background.note: Pilgrims needed unblemished animals and temple coinage, which traders supplied at a markup.

Jhn.3.occasion: Nicodemus by night and the Baptist's final testimony.
Jhn.3.structure: New birth from above, the wind and the Spirit, the love of God, and John's decline.
Jhn.3.world_behind: A Pharisee and member of the ruling council came at night, when private teaching was normal.

deep_background.note: The Greek phrase means both again and from above, which is why Nicodemus misunderstands.

Jhn.4.occasion: The Samaritan woman and the official's son.
Jhn.4.structure: The well at Sychar, living water, the woman's testimony, and the healing at a distance.
Jhn.4.world_behind: Jacob's well was deep, and drawing water was women's daily work at the cooler hours.

deep_background.note: Samaritans worshipped on Mount Gerizim, and the dispute over the right place is the pivot.

Jhn.5.occasion: Healing at Bethesda and the sabbath dispute.
Jhn.5.structure: The pool healing, the charge of sabbath breaking, and the discourse on the Father's testimony.
Jhn.5.world_behind: The pools by the Sheep Gate drew the sick, hoping for moving water and healing.

deep_background.note: Calling God his Father made the claim of shared work and shared authority, which drew the charge.

Jhn.6.occasion: Feeding the five thousand and the bread of life.
Jhn.6.structure: The sign on the hillside, walking on the water, and the discourse in the Capernaum synagogue.
Jhn.6.world_behind: Barley loaves were the cheap bread of the poor, and a boy carried the crowd's lunch.

deep_background.note: The crowd cites the wilderness bread, so Jesus answers with himself as the true bread.

Jhn.7.occasion: The Feast of Tabernacles and the divided crowds.
Jhn.7.structure: The brothers' challenge, secret arrival, teaching in the temple, the water ceremony, and the officers sent to arrest him.
Jhn.7.world_behind: Tabernacles drew pilgrims to Jerusalem and included a daily water-pouring rite at the altar.

deep_background.note: The cry on the last day answers the water libation the crowd had just watched.

Jhn.8.occasion: The woman caught and the light of the world.
Jhn.8.structure: The trap in the temple court, the withdrawal of the accusers, the light discourse, and the claim before Abraham.
Jhn.8.world_behind: Stoning was a public sentence, and the temple courts were where teachers settled legal questions.

deep_background.note: The phrase echoes the divine name in Exodus, which is why the hearers take up stones.

Jhn.9.occasion: The man born blind receives sight and is expelled.
Jhn.9.structure: The healing with clay, the neighbours' confusion, the interrogation, the expulsion, and the worship.
Jhn.9.world_behind: Spittle and clay were common folk remedies, and blindness was assumed to be punishment for sin.

deep_background.note: The pool's name means sent, which the narrator ties to the one who sent Jesus.

Jhn.10.occasion: The good shepherd discourse at the Feast of Dedication.
Jhn.10.structure: Sheep and shepherd, the hired hand, the other sheep, the charge of blasphemy, and the withdrawal across the Jordan.
Jhn.10.world_behind: Dedication commemorated the temple's rededication, and the portico of Solomon sheltered the crowd.

deep_background.note: A hired hand had no stake in the flock, unlike a shepherd who owned the sheep.

Jhn.11.occasion: The raising of Lazarus and the decision to kill Jesus.
Jhn.11.structure: The sisters' message, the delay, Martha's confession, the tomb, the command, and the council's verdict.
Jhn.11.world_behind: Burial followed death within a day, and a cave tomb was sealed with a stone.

deep_background.note: The high priest's counsel that one die for the nation is framed as unwitting prophecy.

Jhn.12.occasion: Anointing, the entry, and the hour of glorification.
Jhn.12.structure: Bethany anointing, the colt and the crowd, the Greeks' request, the grain of wheat, and the voice from heaven.
Jhn.12.world_behind: Pilgrims waved palm branches at Tabernacles and welcomed arriving dignitaries with them.

deep_background.note: The phrase means both crucifixion and exaltation, holding the cross and glory together.

Jhn.13.occasion: The last supper, foot washing, and Judas' departure.
Jhn.13.structure: The washing, Peter's protest, the betrayal foretold, Judas leaving, and the new commandment.
Jhn.13.world_behind: Guests' feet were washed by the lowest servant, since sandals and dusty roads made it necessary.

deep_background.note: Guests lay on couches, so the beloved disciple could lean back against Jesus' chest.

Jhn.14.occasion: The farewell discourse begins with comfort and promise.
Jhn.14.structure: Many rooms, the way and the truth, Philip's request, the promise of the Advocate, and the gift of peace.
Jhn.14.world_behind: A household's inner rooms were the family's secure space, an image of belonging.

deep_background.note: The word describes a legal helper called alongside, a defence in court.

Jhn.15.occasion: The vine and branches, and the world's hatred.
Jhn.15.structure: Vinedresser and pruning, abiding in love, chosen friendship, and the world's opposition.
Jhn.15.world_behind: Vineyards were pruned hard each season, and unfruitful wood was burned.

deep_background.note: Calling servants friends shifts the relationship from command to shared counsel.

Jhn.16.occasion: Sorrow turned to joy and the Spirit's work.
Jhn.16.structure: Persecution foretold, the Advocate's conviction, the little while, the woman in labour, and peace in tribulation.
Jhn.16.world_behind: Synagogue expulsion was a formal social penalty, not merely a disagreement.

deep_background.note: The phrase confuses the disciples because it can mean both a short time and a small amount.

Jhn.17.occasion: The high priestly prayer of Jesus.
Jhn.17.structure: Glorification, the disciples kept, unity among believers, and the world's belief through them.
Jhn.17.world_behind: Prayer with eyes lifted and hands open was a common posture for blessing and petition.

deep_background.note: The word belongs to temple setting-apart, tying the disciples' mission to sacrifice.

Jhn.18.occasion: The arrest and the trials before Annas and Pilate.
Jhn.18.structure: The garden arrest, Peter's denial, the hearing before Annas, and the interrogation by Pilate.
Jhn.18.world_behind: The Kidron valley lay between the city and the Mount of Olives, a short walk after supper.
